routes.label: Write both terms as multiples of the same radical

question: The expression \(\sqrt{\dfrac43}-\sqrt{\dfrac34}\) is equal to:
solution:
Rewrite both terms as multiples of \(\sqrt3\), so we can subtract their coefficients. Using the positive square roots,
\[
\sqrt{\frac43}
=\frac2{\sqrt3}
=\frac{2\sqrt3}{3},
\qquad
\sqrt{\frac34}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sqrt{\frac43}-\sqrt{\frac34}
&=\left(\frac23-\frac12\right)\sqrt3\\
&=\frac16\sqrt3.
\end{aligned}
\]
The value is \(\sqrt3/6\), choice A.
